dream: The card boiled in my sleep, a fever of fifty-two degrees. I pressed down on the wedge until the air felt heavy as wet paper. The wide anchor drifted, lazy and wide, while the flat top melted into nothingness. I built a lid from the memory of a flat stone that never cooled, pressing it over the hot dot. A tree fell sideways, its fat trunk crushing the grass. The wedge slipped, thin and tired, and I woke the air up by pushing harder, trusting the lean even as the stack slid into the empty dark.
